chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who prays with coins in his garment that have images (on them), and he said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.تَمَاثِيلُ: Images or statues (often referring to figures of living beings), a key term in discussions of prayer validity regarding clothing.
key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ: Coins (specifically dirhams), referring to currency carried on the person.
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible, a common legal ruling formula.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray with coins that have images on them in your pocket?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of *tamasheel* (images) in prayer attire applies primarily to prominent, standalone depictions of living beings, whereas images on coins embedded in clothing are considered incidental and do not invalidate the prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the image itself and its context, emphasizing that minor or functional imagery does not constitute a barrier to valid worship.
